summary: This bill delays scheduled Medicaid disproportionate share hospital payment reductions by amending the Social Security Act to shift the reduction periods from 2026-2028 to 2029-2031.

scores.thoughts: The bill delays scheduled reductions in Medicaid DSH payments from 2026-2028 to 2029-2031. This maintains higher levels of federal Medicaid spending for a longer period rather than allowing the reductions to take effect, directly expanding or preserving government outlays.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.

The legislation directly amends Medicaid statute to preserve DSH payments to hospitals serving low-income patients. This supports continued public-program funding within the Medicaid system rather than shifting toward private or market-based mechanisms.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration policy, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions address abortion access, funding restrictions, or reproductive health services.
No provisions affect military or defense spending.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy production.
DSH payments support hospitals that disproportionately serve Medicaid and uninsured low-income patients. Delaying the payment reductions preserves this component of the social safety net.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-abuse programs.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
By postponing spending reductions, the bill increases near-term federal outlays and therefore contributes to larger deficits and debt accumulation rather than prioritizing debt reduction.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights measures.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address labor unions, worker protections, or collective bargaining.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
The bill delays scheduled Medicaid DSH payment reductions by three years, directly increasing federal outlays compared with current law and thereby forgoing deficit reduction.
By preserving higher Medicaid DSH payments to safety-net hospitals, the bill maintains government funding that supports care for low-income and uninsured patients.
